headline: MP Rumeen Farhana subjected to abusive language in Parliament
summary: The Brahmanbaria-2 independent MP alleged that fellow lawmakers used abusive language against her, claiming it violates parliamentary norms.
details: Brahmanbaria-2 independent MP Rumeen Farhana alleged that she was subjected to abusive language by other MPs in the parliament yesterday.
The incident occurred while she was speaking on the Bank Resolution (Amendment) Bill, during which ruling party MPs created an uproar.
Rumeen stated that the behavior she witnessed is not expected in the democratic parliament of a country and does not fall within parliamentary norms.
She argued that if there were counter-arguments to her statements, they should have been delivered through proper parliamentary procedures rather than abuse.
Speaker Hafiz Uddin Ahmad responded by urging both ruling and opposition lawmakers not to obstruct their counterparts while speaking.
The Speaker acknowledged Rumeen's sentiment and emphasized the importance of freedom of speech in the parliament.
Rumeen also recalled a similar disgraceful situation she faced in the 2018 parliament when she spoke for the BNP in an Awami League-led house.
She expressed concern that if there is no minimum change in behavior, there is little point in the opposition's presence in the house.
caption:

headline_marked: Parliament [[passes law to replace RAB with SRB]], abolishing the elite force
headline: Parliament passes law to replace RAB with SRB, abolishing the elite force
summary: The Special Response Battalion (SRB) Bill 2026 was passed by voice vote, though opposition members argue the new unit is simply a rebranding of the former force.
details: The government has passed legislation abolishing the Rapid Action Battalion (Rab) and establishing the Special Response Battalion (SRB), a new specialised police unit.
The SRB Bill 2026 was passed in parliament by voice vote following a discussion. The move comes after years of widespread criticism and US sanctions against Rab for serious human rights violations.

Opposition members, including Leader of the Opposition Shafiqur Rahman and Jamaat MPs, slammed the bill, calling it 'old wine in a new bottle'. They argue that the SRB mirrors Rab in structure, personnel, and logistics.
Critics claim that transferring Rab's personnel, offices, powers, and assets to the SRB will leave cases of enforced disappearances and other crimes vulnerable to flawed investigations.

Home Minister Salahuddin Ahmed defended the move, stating that the bill fulfills a pledge to abolish Rab and that state resources, including weapons and intelligence gear, must be preserved by transferring them to the new unit.
The opposition also raised concerns over the lack of clear guidelines on detention facilities and demanded that the grievance redress committee be headed by a former judge.
caption:
